statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-44172 is a flaw in MariaDB Connector/C (libmariadb): mysql_real_escape_string() mishandled the big5 character set, so an application that escaped untrusted input with it and sent the query over the text protocol on a big5 connection was open to SQL injection (GHSA-pv9p-5w55-55jm, https://github.com/MariaDB/server/security/advisories/GHSA-pv9p-5w55-55jm, CONC-819). The advisory lists Connector/C 3.3.1 to 3.3.18 and 3.4.1 to 3.4.8 as affected and 3.3.19 and 3.4.9 as fixed. The fix is commit https://github.com/mariadb-corporation/mariadb-connector-c/commit/1f168de4e09838ffe14da061142ed387541aa25d, which makes the big5 lead-byte and trail-byte checks in libmariadb/ma_charset.c compare unsigned bytes. The MariaDB server source bundles Connector/C as its libmariadb submodule, and MariaDB lists this CVE among the security fixes of 11.4.11 and 11.8.7, released on 18 May 2026. The Connector/C copy bundled with MariaDB 11.4.9 is 3.4.8; the copy bundled with 11.4.10 does not contain the fix commit, although its build files already say 3.4.9; 11.4.11 is the first 11.4 release whose copy contains it. Alpine records the fix at mariadb 11.4.11-r0 in its 3.23 security database (https://secdb.alpinelinux.org/v3.23/main.json). The Alpine mariadb build removes the shared libmariadb.so library (Alpine ships that in its separate mariadb-connector-c package), but the client programs link the bundled copy statically. We checked every mariadb build published in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository as of 2026-11-28, 11.4.9-r0, 11.4.10-r0, 11.4.11-r0, 11.4.12-r0, 11.4.13-r0 and 11.4.14-r0, on x86_64 and aarch64: /usr/bin/mariadb-dump in each build's mariadb-client package has no libmariadb.so entry in its NEEDED list and carries Connector/C's _client_version connection attribute and the big5 character-set name, and /usr/bin/mariadb-backup in each build's mariadb-backup package carries the MariaDB version string that matches its package version (11.4.9-MariaDB to 11.4.14-MariaDB). 11.4.11-r0 is the first build on a MariaDB release whose bundled Connector/C includes the fix, so the range ends there and the earlier builds are affected.

statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-44172 is a flaw in MariaDB Connector/C (libmariadb): mysql_real_escape_string() mishandled the big5 character set, so an application that escaped untrusted input with it and sent the query over the text protocol on a big5 connection was open to SQL injection (GHSA-pv9p-5w55-55jm, https://github.com/MariaDB/server/security/advisories/GHSA-pv9p-5w55-55jm, CONC-819). The advisory lists Connector/C 3.3.1 to 3.3.18 and 3.4.1 to 3.4.8 as affected and 3.3.19 and 3.4.9 as fixed. The fix is commit https://github.com/mariadb-corporation/mariadb-connector-c/commit/1f168de4e09838ffe14da061142ed387541aa25d, which makes the big5 lead-byte and trail-byte checks in libmariadb/ma_charset.c compare unsigned bytes. The MariaDB server source bundles Connector/C as its libmariadb submodule, and MariaDB lists this CVE among the security fixes of 11.4.11 and 11.8.7, released on 18 May 2026. Debian fixes it in trixie with mariadb 1:11.8.8-0+deb13u1 (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-44172). Every mariadb build published in the DHI Debian repository as of 2026-11-28 is one of four DHI rebuilds of Debian's mariadb 1:11.8.6-0+deb13u1, each with 56 binary packages per architecture including the -dbgsym packages, on amd64 and arm64. Debian builds Connector/C from the copy bundled with the server: in all four builds on both architectures, the libmariadb3 package ships libmariadb.so.3, which exports mysql_real_escape_string, and /usr/bin/mariadb-dump in the mariadb-client package links its own static copy (no libmariadb.so.3 entry in its NEEDED list). The Connector/C copy bundled with MariaDB 11.8.6 does not contain the fix commit, although its build files already say 3.4.9; 11.8.7 is the first 11.8 release whose copy contains it. The Debian changelog shipped in the libmariadb3 package of all four builds on both architectures does not mention this CVE or CONC-819. Every published build is therefore affected until the owner ships MariaDB 11.8.7 or later, or a backport of the fix.
